gen-gf-baumans-gf-inria-sans: Distinctive at first glance, Baumans opens its c like a crescent wrench and makes the headline do the talking. Inria Sans, with tubular strokes like bent copper pipe, does the quieter work of staying see-through.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-istok-web: Modern yet stern, Baumans shows stencil-cut letters of one steady width up top. Istok Web, a sans of rounded forms whose side stays clearly open, does the friendlier talking.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-jost: Wrench-wide and hard to miss: Baumans opens its c like a crescent wrench, every stroke the same weight. Jost steps in with broad terminal gaps and a unit-width stroke, which lets the heading speak first.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-jura: Jura holds its strokes as constant as bent wire beneath Baumans and its crescent-wrench c. And over a full column its s curves, open wide at both ends, keep the text moving without snagging.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-k2d: Clean and tube-like, K2D keeps its thickness through every bend, its c terminals hanging far from the bowl. Baumans above it is the loud one, a commanding display face with a c like a crescent wrench.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-kanchenjunga: Crisp as a technical drafting pen, the text under Baumans never clogs at low resolution. Kanchenjunga would carry paragraph after paragraph in that same unbroken line, leaving the loud work to the heading.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-kantumruy-pro: Baumans swings its c open like a crescent wrench, a commanding display heading with distinctive, uniformly thick strokes. Loud meets friendly, since Kantumruy Pro's e opens clearly rightward.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-kodchasan: Baumans is distinctive and commanding, its c gaping like a crescent wrench. Kodchasan, with terminals that hang open and no calligraphic thinning, does the quiet job of carrying the words.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-koho: KoHo, a sans-serif with wide c apertures, keeps text clean while Baumans swings its own c open like a wrench. Both fonts open their c, one loudly and one quietly.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-kosugi: Kosugi has an open-jawed c like a pair of pliers. That wire-bent look carries across whole words in this plain sans, so paragraphs below Baumans and its crescent-wrench c read steadily and cleanly.
